title: Day 3 — Digital Inputs & the Oscilloscope
_comment: Day 3 in-class deck, following the prototyped PowerPoint slide-for-slide.
Content slides (ref) pull a hidden <slide> block or an activity out of the
book by xml:id (one source of truth); title/section/agenda/notice slides are
in-class glue. presenterNote fields are instructor-only (timing, reveal cues)
and are not projected. The three port-bit diagram slides (basic structure,
switch-connects, input config) carry no bullets, so the deck renders each
figure large. Solution listings (9-11) are projected but are instructor
material; keep them out of any student handout.

slides.title: Reminder: Late Lab Assignment Policy
items: Each student has 2 late days, used at your discretion for lab assignments — say so in a submission comment.
Submit within 24 hours of the deadline using a late day → no penalty.
Otherwise: late labs accepted up to two days late (due date adjusted for used late days) at 10% per day.
After two days beyond the deadline, lab assignments are not accepted for credit.

slides.title: Reminder: Labs and the Honor Code
items: You work alone on the labs unless we specifically say otherwise.
Interaction while learning is encouraged — but exchange ideas, not code. The work you turn in must be your own.
Copying any portion of another person's code (or a design posted online / from another course) violates the Honor Principle.
Always cite your lab and study partners by name.

slides.title: Reminder: AI Use in ENGS 28
items: You may use the HiTA tool (in Canvas). Do not use other GenAI tools unless explicitly invited.
Give notice that you used an AI tool, and how, in your code comments and lab report.
If you base work on generated code, test it and adapt it to the assignment and to your own understanding.
You must understand any code you submit and be able to explain it. All comments must be in your own words.
